findings.question: Q4
findings.title: A returned account handing interrupted before buffer registration is forgotten, allowing a second simulated execution after restore

steps: Build the existing synthetic battery fixture, following BudgetReader and ExecutionDesk gateway; retain the original BudgetLedger checkpoint with BudgetLedger.from_dict.
Dispatch the admitted simulate_pulse action once; the executor appends run.1 through ordinary BudgetLedger.settle.

Call reader.pinned with a one-shot line trace raising KeyboardInterrupt at pinned line 974, 976 or 977. accounts() has returned the live native account dictionaries and their ledger holds the settled spend.
The pin propagates KeyboardInterrupt. The cleanup checks only membership in _uncompared; the returned mapping was not registered, so neither a pending handing nor an unread spend remains.
Replace o.ledgers[lid] with the original checkpoint via normal dictionary assignment; dispatch the same previously admitted action through gateway.dispatch.

findings.actual_result: Each of the three checkpoints produced calls=2, refused=false, pending_before_restore={}, unread_before_restore={}, sealed=null and no diverged account. This is an actual second executor invocation, not merely a successful reader return.
findings.expected_result: The interrupted verification must preserve or fail closed on the account state it was already handed. Restoring an earlier checkpoint after that handed spend must not reauthorize the same admitted action; executor count remains one.
findings.trust_boundary: The line tracer is deterministic fault scheduling, not a proposer-side authority change. It injects KeyboardInterrupt at an interruptible production transition and does not rewrite the ledger or mint an action. All account settlement, checkpoint replacement and dispatch use existing APIs. Thus this models an execution-side interruption and ordinary restore, not private scientific-state corruption by a proposer.
findings.scope_limit: The exact timing was modeled using sys.settrace, not a real asynchronously delivered OS signal. The returned accounts are nevertheless explicitly confirmed present in frame locals, and all subsequent production recovery/dispatch paths execute unchanged.
findings.proposed_correction: Make the returned-handing lifecycle recoverable before any exception path can return control to the owner. Cleanup must account for a callback result even when ticket registration has not completed; a later pin must not proceed as if no handing occurred. Add deterministic controls at the callback-return and pre-registration boundaries with executor-count assertions.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Twice-interrupted native capture retains a mutable mapping rather than the handed spend, so later recovery accepts the restored account

steps: Create the same synthetic gateway and checkpoint, and dispatch once so the owner account holds the settled run.1.
Temporarily wrap _retain_handing to raise KeyboardInterrupt on exactly its first two entries, then delegate to the real implementation. No source file is changed.

Call reader.pinned. The first interruption occurs after _uncompared[ticket]=mapping but before native entry tuples are captured. Cleanup calls _recover_handing; its retry is the second interrupted capture.
The original interrupt propagates and pending_before_restore reports a tuple (the original pair containing live dictionaries), rather than _RetainedHanding; no unread entry barrier exists.
Restore the owner ledger through o.ledgers[lid]=checkpoint. The raw pending dictionary now points at the restored ledger.
The next gateway.dispatch first recovers the pending tuple using the restored dictionary contents, clears the pending record and executes the same admitted action again.

findings.actual_result: The case produced two explicit retention-entry interruptions, pending_before_restore={4: tuple}, unread_before_restore={}, calls=2 and refused=false. pending_after_dispatch was empty. The paired single-interruption control produced calls=1, refused=true and an unread barrier with two charge entries.
findings.expected_result: Repeated interruption may leave verification pending, but pending recovery must remain bound to the originally handed accounts. A later dictionary-entry replacement must not change what recovery observes or let the recorded spend vanish; executor count remains one.
findings.trust_boundary: The helper wrapper injects only KeyboardInterrupt at a deterministic phase; all ordinary helper behavior is delegated unchanged after two interruptions. This models resource/operator interruption before capture plus cleanup interruption, then normal account checkpoint replacement. No frozen-account mutation, private mint or executor extraction is used.
findings.scope_limit: The two interrupts were injected by a temporary in-memory helper wrapper, not a live OS timing experiment. The observed pending representation and actual second executor invocation establish the state transition under that modeled interruption.
findings.proposed_correction: Do not treat recovery of an uncaptured live mapping as recovery of the earlier handing. Preserve immutable native mapping entry observations through capture/cleanup, or retain an explicit unresolved state that cannot be discharged from changed live mappings. Add a control interrupting _retain_handing itself twice before dictionary-entry replacement; the existing _handed interruption controls begin after capture has succeeded.
